evidence: 2026-09-30: real signup through the Agent Vault proxy using this recipe, with browser egress through the owner's tunnel on a US network. After Continue with email and the address, a Create your account step asked for a name; Continue then showed a code step. With a test-inbox address (agentmail.to) the code step said "Temporary emails can't be used on Canva" and no mail was sent. With an address on the owner's own domain, Canva sent a code, the account owner entered it in a handoff (outcome completed), and the session reached the signed-in Canva home ("What will you design today"). No password was set: sign-in is by emailed code.
gotchas: The page opens on sign-up choices; click 'Continue with email' to show the box (the mode_toggle precondition).
The box's id is generated; its name, username, is stable, and it takes an email address or a phone number.

Stepped and passwordless: the address, then a Create your account step with a name box (role=textbox named Name), then a code sent by email. The code belongs to the account owner: hand it off. No password is set.

Canva refuses addresses it classes as temporary: on 2026-09-30 an agentmail.to address got "Temporary emails can't be used on Canva" on the code step, and no code was sent. The account owner's own domain was accepted.
